title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Jankov-von Neumann uniformization theorem: for Polish spaces X and Y and a nonempty analytic (Sigma-1-1) set P in X x Y, there is a function phi : X -> Y that uniformizes P on its projection, (x, phi x) in P for every x in proj_X(P), and that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable, meaning that phi-preimages of Borel subsets of Y lie in the sigma-algebra generated by the analytic subsets of X.  The statement of record writes both sigma-algebras out in full, so it mentions only Mathlib notions and no bespoke definition: the domain sigma-algebra is MeasurableSpace.generateFrom {s | MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet s} (Bertsekas-Shreve Definition 7.19) and the codomain sigma-algebra is borel Y, given explicitly rather than through an ambient instance.  The proof is Kechris's own argument for 18.1: write the analytic P as the range of a continuous map from Baire space, pull it back to a closed set F in X x (N -> N), uniformize F by the leftmost branch of the section tree, and push forward.  The measurability of the leftmost branch is proved cylinder by cylinder: the preimage of a basic cylinder is a countable Boolean combination of projections of closed sets, hence lies in sigma(Sigma-1-1). Unlike the textbook proof, the Lean development never reduces the domain to Baire space, so the invariance of sigma(Sigma-1-1) under Borel isomorphism is never needed. Neither the theorem nor the analytic sigma-algebra exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  Jankov-von Neumann is the selection engine of that development: it is what produces the sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable epsilon-optimal strategies.
